brief:
I'm looking for related work for a paper I'm writing. Our central question is how firms adjust to minimum wage increases when they face monopsonistic labour markets — specifically whether wage compression in the lower tail of the distribution causes changes in employment composition, not just employment levels. We use German administrative data matched employer-employee records and exploit regional variation in the 2015 minimum wage introduction.

What are the key papers in this literature?

What are the key papers studying the role of job search frictions and directed search in explaining wage dispersion across workers with similar observable skills? I'm especially interested in papers that connect Burdett-Mortensen wage posting to empirical wage distributions.
climate change adaptation and labour market outcomes — worker mobility, local labour markets, migration, stranded industries

David Autor's papers and papers that build directly on his work — I want to understand the arc of his research agenda on tasks, polarisation, robots, and trade with China. Include papers responding to or extending his findings.

which labour economics papers were published in the top five general-interest economics journals (AER, QJE, JPE, REStud, Econometrica) in the last five years? I want to understand what topics are considered top-journal worthy right now.

most cited papers on the employment effects of minimum wage increases — I want the classics, the controversial Card-Krueger work, and the more recent literature using bunching or border discontinuity designs
behavioral economics papers on retirement savings and pension decisions — nudges, automatic enrollment, default effects, present bias in pension contributions

papers studying the employment effects of the German minimum wage introduction in 2015 — I want both the early regional impact studies and the later papers that have longer panels and can identify dynamic effects

papers applying regression discontinuity design to labour market questions — not the methodological RDD papers themselves but substantive applications in labour economics that use RDD as their primary identification strategy
